title: AMC and Regal Back Paramount-WBD Merger, Warn Against Costly Antitrust Trial
text:
Regal and AMC CEOs publicly support the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, citing commitments from Paramount CEO David Ellison. They caution against a lengthy antitrust trial, while Cinema United and other opponents remain skeptical. The deal could reshape Hollywood's theatrical future.
The biggest theater chains in America have chosen a side in Hollywood's most heated merger battle, with Regal and AMC publicly endorsing the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros.
Discovery deal while cautioning against a costly and prolonged antitrust trial. Regal CEO Eduardo Acuna issued an exclusive statement urging all stakeholders to reach an agreement rather than proceed with the scheduled March 2027 antitrust trial. Acuna warned that a lengthy court battle creates more uncertainty and distraction that could be damaging to the industry. He revealed direct conversations with Paramount CEO David Ellison, who made a series of commitments aimed at reassuring the exhibition sector.
Ellison pledged at least 30 theatrical releases per year, guaranteed theatrical windows including 45 days for TVOD and 90 days for SVOD, and a staggering $30 billion yearly content spend. Acuna expressed confidence in Ellison's sincerity, adding that Ellison voluntarily offered to sign a consent decree with state attorneys general to further solidify his promises.
AMC CEO Adam Aron also voiced his support in a July 29 Variety column, dismissing the antitrust case as misguided and arguing that the complaint simply gets the economics of the exhibition business backwards. With both leading global theater chains now aligned in favor of the merger, the industry is closely watching the legal and regulatory battles ahead. Despite this strong backing from the exhibition giants, opposition remains fierce.
Cinema United CEO Michael O'Leary continues to oppose the acquisition, expressing concerns that the merger could lead to a decline in theatrical product similar to what was observed after the Disney-Fox merger. O'Leary noted that Paramount went silent after Cinema United submitted its concerns on July 1, raising questions about the transparency of the deal-making process.
TKO Group Holdings CEO Ari Emanuel also weighed in, championing the deal in a Wall Street Journal column where he labeled the antitrust suit as trash and insisted that the merger could save Hollywood. The 2026 domestic box office has already surpassed $6 billion, reaching its highest point since 2019, which adds a layer of complexity to the debate.
Top Gun: Maverick producer Jerry Bruckheimer shared his optimism about Ellison's commitments at the Producers Guild Awards, and later added at CinemaCon that the merger train has left the station. Cinemark CEO Sean Gamble similarly praised the prospect of increased theatrical investment during the Morgan Stanley conference, suggesting that a combined Paramount-WBD entity could revitalize the industry. The merger has faced significant legal hurdles, including a temporary halt by a federal judge and ongoing proceedings in California federal court.
As the legal battle unfolds, the future of the deal remains uncertain. However, the support from major theater chains carries considerable weight, as their cooperation is essential for the success of any major studio merger. Ellison's commitments, if honored, would represent a significant boost for theaters, which have struggled to recover from the pandemic-era disruptions. The merger's outcome will not only shape the landscape of Hollywood but also determine the fate of countless jobs and creative projects.
With box office numbers climbing and industry leaders divided, the next few months will be crucial. The March 2027 trial date looms large, but many hope that a settlement can be reached before then. As Acuna emphasized, the industry needs certainty and focus, not a protracted legal fight that could harm everyone involved. The clock is ticking, and the decisions made in the coming weeks could redefine the entertainment industry for years to come
